test: Official Goose UI/native GPU memory isolation

source.hash_note: Final probe includes all isolation modes. Runs used successive probe revisions as modes were added; the final source reproduces each mode. No game source was edited by the investigator.

measured_facts: Retaining both UI GPU buffers grew maximum RSS from 246,890,496 bytes at 1,000 frames to 633,044,992 bytes at 3,000 frames. Native UI texture and GPU buffer capacity counters remained fixed.
Recreating either the vertex or index GPU buffer each frame removed the observed growth. Recreating both also worked.
Retiring only the index buffer remained bounded for 3,000 pipelined frames without gfx::flush. This mode sleeps 1 ms per frame and is not a throughput benchmark.
Keeping both UI buffers but creating/releasing an unrelated 16-byte GPU buffer each frame also removed the growth.
Exact-sized uploads and disabling graphics validation did not remove the growth.
Generated C for ui::render resets all three temporary Goose stack tops on return. Unchanged-scale font baking returns immediately; native UI command/conversion buffers clear each frame.

native_inference.conclusion: Evidence points to native SDL/Metal command-buffer or staging-resource cleanup timing, rather than Goose entity collections, UI font rebaking, or unreclaimed ui::render scratch.
native_inference.caveat: The exact native defect was not proven. Buffer retirement and the sentinel introduce fresh native submissions/destruction, either of which can change cleanup timing. Do not describe this as an index-format-specific leak.
native_inference.streaming_test_caveat: The long GPU streaming workload released terrain buffers every 20 frames; that intervention can mask this static-scene native growth. The full app therefore needs its own post-workaround memory test.

official_source_findings.fact: input_begin ends and clears the previous drawn frame.
Conversion command, vertex and index buffers are cleared before reuse.
Each buffer upload creates a transfer buffer and releases it at line 124.
Command-buffer cleanup drops references to used resources.
Submit cleans completed command buffers, then performs pending destruction.
WaitForFences performs pending destruction after waiting.

workaround.scope: UI GPU resource retirement only; no game storage/allocator changes
workaround.after: Render all UI contexts, then retire/reset the shared index buffer once.
workaround.portability_note: Measured on the pinned macOS Metal backend. Other backends were not tested.

measurement_notes: All reported maxima include native graphics driver allocations and process teardown.
macOS peak memory footprint differs from RSS and is preserved as a separate counter.
A finite probe and bounded counters do not prove absence of every native leak.
The text log is a faithful transcription of selected captured output fields, not a byte-for-byte saved subprocess stream.
The 3,000-frame UI runs differ in submission pacing; matching 1,000-frame synchronous runs isolate the retirement intervention. Full application before/after testing is separate.
